detail.title: Architectural Distinctions in Preference Formation
detail.summary: This provisional notebook explores the distinction between transient behavioral states and stable preference formation. It suggests that while transient behaviors are reactive to immediate environment variables, preference formation—or stable risk attitudes—requires architectural encoding, as evidenced by risk-sensitive MPC frameworks and adversarial interaction models.
